runs.text: ſinal de ter que comer, & estar proſpero.

lines.note: Continues f414's cooking-smoke example: the smoke is a sign of having food and being prosperous. The matching catchword on f414 is not duplicated as body text there.

runs.text: Preſente com que ſe viſita alguem.

lines.note: Reimot is a gift taken when visiting someone. The scan reads viſita, correcting the draft's transposed viſtia.
Reiqen denotes an excellent or wondrous sword. The Portuguese comparison begins with co-mo, continued below.

runs.text: mo a dos Reis antiguos. Vt,

lines.note: The sword is compared with those of ancient kings. Tencano rei- begins the Japanese example, continued into qen on the next row; the historical spelling antiguos is retained.
Tencano reiqen and the alternative busǒno reiqen identify a supremely excellent sword. The Portuguese superlative is divided at excelẽ-te; the printed short s in busǒno remains unchanged.
Completes the superlative as the most excellent sword of all. The short physical row belongs to the preceding Reiqen example.
This Reiqi is a soul or spirit. It is distinct from the homonymous turtle entry immediately below.
The second Reiqi is a tortoise or turtle whose markings have significance. Printed Cagado is preserved without adding a modern accent.

runs.text: vincos que tem nas costas, vendo hum homem

lines.note: The markings and grooves on the animal's back were observed by a man. The subject and the resulting knowledge continue on the next row; the provisional st classification in costas is retained.

runs.text: antiguo aprendeo muitas couſas de Aſtrologia.

lines.note: Completes the account: an ancient man learned many things about astrology from those markings. This is the dictionary's explanation, without supplying a particular legendary name absent from the print.
Yoi niuoi explains Reiqiǒ as a good or excellent fragrance. The spiritual quality of that fragrance is developed in the following row.
The fragrance is described as almost supernatural. Reiqiǒ yomoni begins the example of its spreading in every direction; ſobre natural retains its printed separation.

runs.text: O bom cheiro recende por todas

lines.note: Cunzu completes the example of fragrance spreading everywhere. The Portuguese reads por todas, not the draft's par todas.
Completes 'in all directions'. This short continuation finishes the Reiqiǒ example.
Reiquǒ denotes a marvelous, almost supernatural radiance. The headword begins with a damaged R, not the draft's F; ma- continues into the adjective below.
Completes marauilhoſa, describing the radiance as wondrous. The row belongs to Reiquǒ rather than to the next entry.
Vochibururu explains falling into decline or ruin. The Portuguese gives becoming damaged, with a further description of deterioration on the next row.
Continues the decline gloss as something progressively being destroyed or becoming worse. The historical empeyorando and the provisional st ligature reading in destruindo remain unchanged.

runs.text: Adu. Modo de eſtar, ou correr a-

lines.note: Reirei is labeled adverbial and first describes the condition or flow of cold water. The a- begins agoa on the next physical row.

runs.text: goa fria. ¶ Item, Modo de voz ſonoro,

lines.note: Completes agoa fria, then adds a description of a resonant voice or sound. The following row supplies the quality brando and its musical example.
The sound is resonant and gentle. Quanguenno coye reirei-tari describes the sound of instrumental music; the word is physically divided after reirei-.

runs.text: As vozes da muſica, ou deſcante ſoa-

lines.note: Completes reireitari. The Portuguese refers to musical or ensemble voices sounding; the worn c in deſcante is recovered from the crop rather than left as the draft's deſante.

runs.text: uão com hum tom alto, ſonoro, & brando.

lines.note: Completes ſoa-uão and describes a high, resonant, gentle tone. The historical spelling of the verb is preserved rather than modernized.

runs.text: Couſa de habilidade, ou engenho. S.

lines.note: Reiri describes ability or ingenuity. The draft's grave accent in Couſà is not supported by the crop; the final S is an upright register label. Typeface update: S. is provisionally italicized under the bulk convention.

runs.text: Couſas lucidas que estão enfiadas, & por

lines.note: Reirô describes bright things arranged in a string or orderly sequence. The examples continue below; the circumflex and the provisional st form in estão are retained.

runs.text: ordem como pedras precioſas, ou muitas lu-

lines.note: The orderly bright things are compared with precious stones or many lights. Lu- is the beginning of the next row's lumieiras, not a Japanese fragment.
Completes the historical Portuguese lumieiras, lights or illuminations. The spelling is preserved rather than replaced with a modern equivalent.
Fiyai mizzu identifies cold water. The crop shows both the word space and the doubled z, correcting the draft's Fiyaimizu without normalizing the Japanese spelling.
Cristalina completes the description of cold water as pure and crystal-clear. The provisional st classification remains unchanged.
Reitai denotes a wondrous or spiritual substance or entity. The historical Suſtancia is retained, without adding the b of modern substância.
The soul is offered as an example of that spiritual substance. This short continuation closes Reitai.

runs.text: Couſa deſabrida, & que não tẽ ſabor.

lines.note: Reitan describes something insipid or lacking taste. The headword's R corrects the draft's F, and the nasal abbreviation in tẽ is retained.
Suſamajij ſora describes a chilly sky or atmosphere. The crop confirms the Suſamajij sequence that is more damaged on f414; the Portuguese alternative continues below.
Completes the atmosphere's description as somewhat cold. It is part of Reiten, not the balance entry that follows.

runs.text: Dachem, hũa certa balança com que

lines.note: Reitengu is explained as a particular balance, called Dachem in the Portuguese gloss. Its use is specified on the next row; the loanword is not silently modernized.
The balance is used to weigh silver and similar materials. This completes Reitengu's practical description.
Qidocuna tocu identifies extraordinary benefits or merit. The Portuguese starts 'great or marvelous', with ma- continuing below.
Completes marauilhoſos and gives spiritual benefit or fruit. The visible vi sequence corrects the draft's shortened raulhoſos.
This Reixa is a person paying compliments or respects during a visit. The historical comprimentos and the tilde abbreviation in viſitãdo are retained.
Adds giving thanks as an alternative action of the Reixa. The grave accent in dà is copied rather than modernized.

runs.text: Cami milagroſo, que faz couſas mara-

lines.note: The homonymous Reixa is explained as a miraculous Cami. Cami occurs inside the Portuguese definition. Its slanted lowercase forms match the following italic prose on the second pass, so that type is retained and the whole word is also listed for font review.

runs.text: uilhoſas ſendo rogado, ao parecer dos homẽs.

lines.note: Completes marauilhoſas: the Cami is said to do wonders when petitioned, 'in people's opinion'. That qualifying phrase is part of the dictionary's wording and is preserved.
Reino jeni identifies money given in thanks or courtesy. In that Japanese context, Caixas refers to cash coins rather than boxes; the Portuguese begins the description of presenting them.
The cash is presented or offered when visiting someone. This completes the first Reixen definition.

runs.text: Tempos determinados em que ſe fazẽ

lines.note: The second Reixen denotes appointed times for formal courtesies or visits. The headword begins with R, and determinados is a single printed word, correcting the draft.
Completes the appointed-times definition as the occasions for due courtesies and visits. It does not describe the amount of the preceding monetary gift.

runs.text: Caixas que ſe dão de pre

lines.note: Reixiqi is given with reixen as an alternative and refers to cash presented as a gift. The crop restores both headwords and Caixas; pre continues into ſente in the next column, without a securely printed terminal hyphen.
Completes preſente from the other column: cash given as a gift on visiting someone. This is the continuation of Reixiqi, not a new headword.

runs.text: Caſa como oratorio onde ſe poem a fi-

lines.note: This Reixit denotes a room like an oratory. The Portuguese says an image is placed there and divides fi-gura across the physical rows.

runs.text: gura, ou imagem dalgum Cami, ou Fotoque.

lines.note: Completes figura and specifies an image of a Cami or Fotoque. Both Japanese divine designations are embedded in Portuguese prose; their italic lowercase forms agree with the surrounding sentence on the second pass, and the words are separately marked for whole-word typeface review.
The homonymous Reixit is explained by sugureta ſugata, an outstanding appearance or form. The Portuguese description continues below.

runs.text: marauilhoſa figura, ou aparencia de peßoa no-

lines.note: Describes a marvelous figure or the appearance of a noble person. The missing vi in the draft's maraulhoſa is restored from the scan; no- continues into bre below.
Completes nobre and adds a dignified or grave appearance. The final S is the upright written-language label. Typeface update: S. is provisionally italicized under the bulk convention.
Fiyeta ſaqe means chilled sake, rendered as cold wine by the dictionary. The Japanese ſaqe is a headword explanation, not an embedded term requiring separate font marking.
Fiyai cuſuri identifies a cooling or cold medicine. The Portuguese's 'of its own nature' continues on the next row and is not a modern treatment recommendation.
Completes the description of the medicine as cold in its inherent nature. This closes the first Reiyacu entry.
The second Reiyacu is an extraordinary medicine, qidocuna cuſuri. The visible comma after Excelente replaces the draft's full stop and joins the following adjective.
Completes the definition as an excellent and marvelous medicine. The final S is a register label rather than part of the italic description.

runs.text: Renban. i, Amatano fito fanuo ſuyuru.

lines.note: Amatano fito fanuo ſuyuru describes many people putting their signatures or seals to a document. The Portuguese nominalized explanation begins with O and continues below.

runs.text: aßinarenſe muitos em algum papel. Vt,

lines.note: The Portuguese describes many people signing one paper. Vt is italic, but the abbreviated Japanese Rẽ- begins the example in roman type; the draft incorrectly included that fragment in the italic span.
Completes Rẽ-banuo ſuyuru, putting joint signatures or seals on the document. This entire short row is the Japanese example, not Portuguese prose.
Coi xitǒ explains romantic longing. The Portuguese characterizes it as sensual or illicit love; deshonesto is a single printed word, not the draft's des honesto.
Completes ſenſual and gives Fitouo renbo ſuru, loving or desiring someone. The Japanese fito and its visible t correct the draft's Firo.
Completes the translation as loving someone sensually. This closes the Renbo example.
Fachiſuno iqe identifies a lotus pond, rendered as a pond of golfãos. The Japanese botanical reference guides the meaning without replacing the historical Portuguese term.
Renchocu denotes uprightness or rectitude. The synonym is printed Sugui-i with a short internal hyphen; it is retained rather than treated as an OCR space or regularized to a modern adjective.
Renchocuna describes something upright and just. Rẽ- begins the Japanese example in roman type, whereas the Portuguese gloss and pilcrow are italic.

Completes Rẽ-chocuna fito, an upright and just person. A small roman i is printed separately at the far right above the following row; it completes the next row's Renchocun rather than this Portuguese sentence. That omitted fragment is retained in its physical position.
The adverb Renchocuni introduces an example of arranging something rightly. The example's final i is displaced above the line at the far right and is recorded on c2-l021, not silently appended here.
Completes the example as planning or arranging something uprightly. The Portuguese al- continues into gũa; its visible line-end mark is restored from the crop.
Completes algũa couſa, something being arranged rightly. The short row closes the adverbial example.
Sudareno vchi means inside the hanging blinds. The Portuguese eſtei-ras describes the screens or mats involved; the mark over u in Renchǔ is retained.

runs.text: ras que ſe dependurão. ¶ No Ximo, Molher

lines.note: Completes the hanging-blinds sense, then gives a regional usage in Ximo referring to a wife. Ximo is embedded in the Portuguese usage statement and is marked separately for font review.
The regional sense is the wife of a nobleman. This completes the second Renchǔ definition.
Fachiſuno ne identifies the lotus root. The dictionary renders it through golfãos and marks the entry with upright S. Typeface update: S. is provisionally italicized under the bulk convention.

runs.text: Lugar como caualete onde ſe depend u-

lines.note: Rendai is described as a stand or trestle for hanging clothing. The scan gives R and Lugar rather than the draft's B and Laugar; the visible gap in depend u- is retained instead of silently regularizing the word.
Completes depend u-rão and says garments are hung and stored on the stand. The provisional st classification in vestidos remains unchanged.
Tçurane vta explains linked verse. The Portuguese begins a description of verses or songs, dividing cã-tigas across the rows.

runs.text: tigas que fazem muitos enfiadas, & dependẽ-

lines.note: The linked verses are composed by several people and arranged in a dependent sequence. The visible tilde and terminal mark give dependẽ-, not the draft's depende.
Completes dependẽtes and says the verses depend on one another. This finishes the collaborative linked-verse description.
Cuuo tçuranuru means linking verse units. The gloss introduces a kind of verse, continuing ver into ſos without a securely visible line-end hyphen.

runs.text: ſos deſta laya que ſe vſão na China.

lines.note: Completes verſos and specifies that this kind is used in China. The row distinguishes Rengu from the preceding Renga description.
Sudareno foca means outside the blinds. The visible r in Sudareno corrects OCR Sudateno; the Portuguese's screens are further described below.
Completes 'outside the hanging blinds'. The upright S marks the written-language register of Renguai. Typeface update: S. is provisionally italicized under the bulk convention.
Fachiſuno fana identifies the lotus blossom. The dictionary gives rose or flower as Portuguese equivalents, completed by the plant name below.
Completes the phrase as the flower of golfão. This is a botanical continuation of Rengue, not a new entry.
Nori voconǒ points to practiced observance or cultivation. The Portuguese explains training oneself and becoming versed in something, with fa- continuing below.

runs.text: zerſe verſado em letras, ou virtudes. ¶

lines.note: Completes fazerſe verſado in letters or virtues. The Japanese example begins Qiǔ-, with a visible mark over u omitted by the draft; it continues into xu on the next row.
Completes the example describing a person practiced and accomplished in the relevant disciplines. The Portuguese begins the parallel description of an experienced person.
Completes the description as versed in learning or virtues. This closes the Renguiǒ example.

runs.text: Hũa corda à maneira de ſilha com q̃

lines.note: This Renjacu is a carrying cord or harness compared with a girth. The abbreviation q̃ introduces an account of how peddlers use it; the grave accent in à is retained.

runs.text: hũs certos bufurinheiros leuão amarrada às co-

lines.note: Certain peddlers use the cord to carry a box tied to their backs. Co- is the beginning of coſtas below, while bufurinheiros retains the printed historical form.

runs.text: ſtas hũa caixa, em que vão muitas miudezas

lines.note: Completes coſtas and describes a box containing many small wares. Here caixa is a carrying box, unlike the cash-gift Caixas in the Reixen entries.
The small wares are carried for sale. This closes the harness sense of Renjacu; the separate bottom-right Renja- catchword anticipates the next page's homonymous entry.

zones.label: Printed catchword
zones.note: Anticipates Renjacu on f416; not repeated as body text.
